Can women along the supply chain influence handling, shift conditions and the distribution of skilled work and ownership?

title: Insects
oneLine: Explore an insect enterprise from the customer's product requirements back to the production system.
need: Insects can be discussed as food, feed or a way to use organic materials, but those are different businesses with different requirements. The first task is to choose a product and willing buyer, then understand accepted inputs, quality, handling and operating conditions. A circular story alone does not establish a market.
offer: Develop a small business study around an appropriate existing production partner, focused on a clearly defined output. Compare sourcing, processing, customer acceptance and residue handling. Regional women with farming, food or logistics experience could lead the customer conversation and decide whether production, aggregation or a service is the useful opportunity.

firstPilot.title: A buyer-led product specification
steps: Interview a prospective buyer about the product form, quality evidence and purchasing conditions they require.
Choose an existing qualified producer or research partner and map permitted inputs and handling requirements.
Evaluate an authorised sample through appropriate quality testing and customer feedback.
Prepare a full material and labour account, including unsold output and production residues.
firstPilot.deliverable: A buyer specification, sample evaluation and production-partnership brief.

evidence.known: The source lists insects as a closed-loop food theme. It supplies no approved species, feedstock, food product or production facility.
evidence.unknown: Whether a defined output can satisfy a real buyer at a price that covers quality control and consistent supply.
evidence.nextMeasurement: Accepted sample quality, buyer willingness to trial, labour per batch and the complete material balance.

resources: Current food or feed compliance advice
businessModel: Explore contract production, aggregation or a customer-specific product with an established operator before building a facility.
leadershipDecision: Select one market and its quality requirements before committing to a species, substrate or production technology.
risks: A waste input may be unsuitable for the intended product.
Customer acceptance may differ from survey enthusiasm.
Inconsistent batches can undermine supply agreements.
sourceNote: Original concept from 500 Queens VC NEW Long, slide 16; current context from the September 2026 planning document. This expanded brief and pilot are proposed development, not evidence of an operating enterprise or confirmed partnership.
